title: LegacyMind Intermediate Representation (IR) v0.1
description: Normalized, LLM-agnostic representation of one legacy module. Produced by either parse engine (stub: cli/src/parse; production: parser/proleap, ProLeap ANTLR4 on the JVM), consumed by transpiler/ and all four verifier layers. Every node carries a source span so provenance survives end-to-end. This schema is the contract: both engines must emit identical IR for sources inside the stub's subset, and documents must always validate against this file.

files.description: SELECT/FD + OPEN/READ/WRITE/CLOSE. Each FD's single 01 record is lowered into dataDivision.items as ordinary storage and referenced here by name. LINE SEQUENTIAL and INDEXED (VSAM, ACCESS SEQUENTIAL) are lowered; ACCESS RANDOM/DYNAMIC, keyed READ, REWRITE, OPEN I-O/EXTEND, more than one input file, and multiple records per FD are outside the subset and rejected at the frontend. Runtime file semantics are ground-truthed by layer B against the real binary (docs/vsam.md).

assignKind.description: Present when the ASSIGN target is bound EXTERNALLY at run time (a JCL DD on z/OS, DD_<name> in the environment here) rather than being a path in the source. Emitted only for ddnames, so a literal-assigned file leaves the key absent and existing replay-cache keys are unaffected.

recordKey.description: RECORD KEY of an INDEXED file. The file is read in KEY order, which the modern side must impose on itself from a flat seed - the defect class of finding 12.

fileStatus.description: FILE STATUS data item. Deliberately NOT bound by layer C: assuming reads always succeed would make abend paths look infeasible (docs/layer-c-declines.md).

recordWidth.description: Total fixed width of the record in bytes; a re-carving via READ INTO must preserve it exactly.

layout.description: Byte-exact field layout of the record (stage 2b, docs/memory-layout.md), used to bind record fields to input slots in layers A and C.

name.description: Absent only on FILLER slots, which have no name to bind.

decode.description: `filler` is unnamed padding: it occupies bytes and is never bound to an input slot, so it must still appear here or the offsets after it would be wrong.

mode.description: From the OPEN statement; each file must be opened in exactly one mode.

file.description: Source path as given to the parser, forward slashes.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the raw source bytes; anchors the provenance chain.

controlFlow.description: Paragraph-level CFG. Statement-level CFG (needed by Layer C symbolic execution) is a planned extension; PERFORM return edges are not yet modeled.

warnings.description: Anything the parser saw but did not fully model. Must never be silently empty when information was dropped — no hidden failures.

scale.description: Digit positions right of the implied (V) or editing (.) decimal point. Critical for COMP-3 vs BigDecimal equivalence.

then.description: Every item declared in the source carries a span. Only the synthetic INDEXED BY item may omit it, so dropping provenance still fails validation everywhere it matters.

level.description: 1-49 group/elementary levels, or 77 standalone items. 66 (RENAMES) and 88 (condition names) are not representable.

path.description: Dot-qualified path from the 01-level root, e.g. WS-WORK.WS-GROSS-PAY.

filler.description: Storage-only FILLER item. The name is parser-synthesized (FILLER-n), MUST NOT be referenced by any statement, and never enters the declared-name set used for refs extraction.

value.description: VALUE clause literal exactly as written (e.g. ZERO, .225, 'ABC').

redefines.description: REDEFINES target: this item is an alternate view over the same storage.

occurs.description: OCCURS n - fixed table cardinality. OCCURS DEPENDING ON is outside the subset.

occursGroup.description: OCCURS n on a GROUP item: the table cardinality, with the group's leaves flattened per element (O3-flat). Distinct from `occurs`, which is the cardinality of an ELEMENTARY table - the two are carried separately because the flattening changes how layers A and C bind element fields to input slots.

indexName.description: This item IS an index, synthesized from INDEXED BY <name> on an OCCURS clause rather than declared in the source: a level-77 PIC 9(4) DISPLAY item settable with SET. Because it has no source line of its own it carries no `span`, which is the one case where `span` may be absent.

window.description: Byte window (docs/byte-window.md): this leaf is a view of `length` bytes at 1-based `offset` within `of`. Produced by reference modification and by a group REDEFINES over an elementary target.

byteModelled.description: This item holds BYTES, not values: a window can leave a space inside a PIC 9, which no numeric domain can hold. Layers A and B execute it; layer C treats it as OPAQUE and layer D reports it UNRESOLVED, rather than either of them claiming a value (docs/byte-window.md).

performThru.description: PERFORM <target> THRU <thru>: the last paragraph of the range. The performed body is the contiguous source-order paragraph range [target..thru] inclusive. The range is forward-contiguous; backward or non-adjacent ranges are rejected by the parser, never mis-lowered.

operandExpr.description: Stub-level expression: raw normalized text plus the declared data items it references. A full expression AST replaces this when the ProLeap parser lands; refs already enable Layer D data-flow diffing.

name.description: Real COBOL paragraph names are frequently digit-leading (0000-CARDFILE-OPEN), so the leading character is [A-Z0-9]. The two space-bearing forms are SYNTHETIC names the frontend creates for code that has no paragraph of its own: statements before the first paragraph header (MAINLINE PARAGRAPH) and inline PERFORM bodies (INLINE PERFORM <n>). They are enumerated explicitly rather than admitted by a looser pattern, so a genuinely malformed name is still rejected.

rounded.description: COBOL ROUNDED = half-up (away from zero). Divergence from Java HALF_EVEN defaults is a classic migration defect; verifier layers key off this flag.

oneOf.description: CALL of an allowlisted external service that NEVER RETURNS (docs/external-services.md). Terminal like stop-run, but the process result is failure. Only admissible because there is no post-call state to get wrong; any service that returns is rejected. `args` are the USING item names, verified as ordinary storage.
EXIT: a no-op paragraph terminator (flow-neutral for every verifier layer). Only representable because PERFORM THRU is not — an EXIT paragraph cannot be a THRU endpoint here.

GO TO <paragraph>. Representable only as the structured early-exit of an enclosing PERFORM <s> THRU <target> range: `target` is that range's THRU endpoint, itself a pure EXIT terminator, and the GO TO lies lexically within [s..target). The frontend rejects every other shape (backward jumps, GO TO DEPENDING ON, non-exit targets, exits of looping THRU ranges); layers C and D eliminate it into equivalent if/else inside inlineStatements before any execution, so no verifier engine sees a raw GO TO. General GO TO stays outside the subset.
OPEN OUTPUT <file> / CLOSE <file> (file I/O stage 1). Flow-neutral for the symbolic layers; runtime semantics (truncation on OPEN OUTPUT, flush on CLOSE) are ground-truthed by layer B.

WRITE <record> (file I/O stage 1): appends the record's current storage to its FD's file. The record is ordinary storage in dataDivision.items, so the MOVEs populating it are fully modeled; the write itself is flow-neutral for the symbolic layers.

READ <file> AT END ... NOT AT END ... (file I/O stage 2a, docs/record-protocol.md): consumes the next record of a LINE SEQUENTIAL input file into the FD record item; the branches are statement lists. Stage 2a admits exactly one READ site, heading the body of one top-level PERFORM UNTIL loop, over a single-elementary-field record, with no ACCEPT in the module. READ INTO / KEY / INVALID KEY / NEXT RECORD are outside the subset.

A MOVE into a BYTE WINDOW - reference modification with a literal offset and length, TARGET(offset:length) (docs/byte-window.md). Kept distinct from `move` because the receiving area is a byte range, not a value: layers A and B execute it, layer C refuses the obligation and layer D reports the key UNRESOLVED. Offset is 1-based, as written in COBOL.
PERFORM <paragraph> <n> TIMES. The body executes exactly n times (n evaluated once, before the first iteration).

PERFORM <paragraph> UNTIL <cond>, TEST BEFORE semantics only (the COBOL 85 default): the condition is checked before each iteration, so zero iterations are possible. TEST AFTER is rejected by the parser, never mis-lowered.
PERFORM <paragraph> VARYING <var> FROM <from> BY <by> UNTIL <cond>, TEST BEFORE: var := from; while not cond: body; var := var + by. Single control variable (VARYING ... AFTER is rejected).
